title: Roaming, controllers and enterprise access points

videos.script: Walk down a corridor on a video call, and your phone passes three or four access points. {{corridor}} It has to leave one and join the next without the other person noticing. That move is called roaming. {{roam}} Most people assume the network hands the phone over, the way a mobile network does. It does not. On Wi-Fi the client decides when to move, and some clients decide late. {{sticky}} A laptop that clings to a distant access point drags its own data rate down. It also slows down everybody else on that channel, because they all share the same air. {{airtime}} This lesson looks at what the network can do about it. Three amendments to the standard make a roam faster and better informed. {{krv}} Then the three ways to run fifty access points: one at a time, from a controller, or from a vendor's cloud. {{arch}} And two numbers that decide a design before anybody switches anything on. How much airtime the clients need, and how much power the switch can deliver. {{numbers}} There is no radio in this lab. The numbers in this lesson come from small programs you can run yourself. {{run}}
